# doit_customer_subscriptions (Data Source)

Organization-wide subscriptions visible to the caller. Alerts and budgets are listed too; their entries have type `alert` or `budget` and no schedule. Without `max_results` every page is fetched; with it, a single page is returned together with the `page_token` of the next one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    doit = {
      source = "doitintl/doit"
    }
  }
}

# List every subscription visible to the caller. All pages are fetched unless
# max_results is set. Alerts and budgets are listed too; their entries have
# type "alert" or "budget" and no schedule.
data "doit_customer_subscriptions" "all" {}

locals {
  # Subscriptions that deliver a report.
  report_subscriptions = [
    for s in data.doit_customer_subscriptions.all.items : s
    if contains([for e in s.subscriptions : e.type], "report-subscription")
  ]
}

output "subscription_names" {
  value = [for s in data.doit_customer_subscriptions.all.items : s.name]
}

output "report_subscription_ids" {
  value = [for s in local.report_subscriptions : s.id]
}

# Read a single page of up to 10 subscriptions; page_token holds the token of
# the next page.
data "doit_customer_subscriptions" "first_page" {
  max_results = 10
}

output "next_page_token" {
  value = data.doit_customer_subscriptions.first_page.page_token
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `max_results` (Number) The maximum number of results to return in a single page. Use the page tokens to iterate through the entire collection.
- `page_token` (String) Page token, returned by a previous call, to request the next page of results
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) Subscriptions ordered by `id` ascending. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))
- `row_count` (Number) Total number of subscriptions visible to the caller. The same value is returned on every page.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `created_by` (String) Email address of the subscription creator. On create, the caller.
- `etag` (String) Opaque version token for optimistic concurrency. 64 lowercase hex characters when set. The response `ETag` header is this value wrapped in double quotes. Send `If-Match: "<etag>"`. `null` only on a dry-run create. It only covers fields this API can write.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned subscription id. `null` only on a dry-run create.
- `name` (String) Display name. For a scheduled subscription, `{source name}` plus `(Dashboard Subscription)`, `(Report Subscription)`, or `(Commitment Subscription)`, from the nested type that sorts first. For an alert or a budget, the source name.
- `recipients` (Attributes) Delivery targets shared by every nested subscription on this item. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--recipients))
- `subscriptions` (Attributes Set) Nested subscriptions ordered by `type` ascending. The server sorts them. One entry per visible type. A scheduled subscription has one, two, or three scheduled types. An alert or a budget has exactly one entry. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--subscriptions))

<a id="nestedatt--items--recipients"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.recipients`

Read-Only:

- `emails` (List of String) Email destinations in stored order. Reads return each address trimmed and lowercase. Addresses must belong to the organization's approved domains and must be a user or a pending invite. `doit.com` and `doit-intl.com` pass the domain check. A blank email, an email with no domain, or a domain the tenant does not allow is refused with `422` and code `DOMAIN_NOT_APPROVED`. An email that is not a user or a pending invite is refused with `422` and code `NOT_INVITED_USER`. The same email twice, ignoring case, is refused with `422` and code `customers.duplicate_recipient`. An address already stored, and still present, is not checked again.
- `slack_channels` (List of String) Slack channel ids in stored order. Reads return the public id. Ids are compared exactly after trim. A duplicate id is refused with `422` and code `customers.duplicate_recipient`. A blank or unconnected id is refused with `422` and code `SLACK_CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`. This API does not list eligible channels.


<a id="nestedatt--items--subscriptions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.subscriptions`

Read-Only:

- `attachments` (List of String) Files to attach to the report subscription email. Present only for `report-subscription`. Always an array on read. Empty means no file. Rejected on any other type with `422`.
- `pdf_settings` (Attributes) PDF rendering options. Present only for `report-subscription`. Always present on a report read. Rejected on any other type with `422`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--subscriptions--pdf_settings))
- `permissions` (Attributes) Actions the authenticated caller may perform on this nested subscription. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--subscriptions--permissions))
- `schedule` (Attributes) Delivery schedule. Omitted for an alert or a budget. Never `null`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--subscriptions--schedule))
- `source` (Attributes) Source resource for this nested subscription. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--subscriptions--source))
- `type` (String) Kind of nested subscription.

<a id="nestedatt--items--subscriptions--pdf_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.subscriptions.pdf_settings`

Read-Only:

- `include_annotations` (Boolean) Include annotations in the PDF time range.
- `include_table` (Boolean) Include the data table in the PDF.
- `show_filters` (Boolean) Include the report filters summary in the PDF.


<a id="nestedatt--items--subscriptions--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.subscriptions.permissions`

Read-Only:

- `can_delete` (Boolean) Whether the caller may delete this subscription. Always `false` for an alert or a budget.
- `can_edit_recipients` (Boolean) Whether the caller may replace recipients.
- `can_unsubscribe` (Boolean) Whether the caller may remove their own recipient email.


<a id="nestedatt--items--subscriptions--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.subscriptions.schedule`

Read-Only:

- `custom_period_amount` (Number) Number of `customPeriodUnit` between deliveries. Present only when `frequency` is `Custom`. At least 1.
- `custom_period_unit` (String) Unit for `customPeriodAmount`. Present only when `frequency` is `Custom`.
- `frequency` (String) Console delivery frequency.
- `next_at` (String) Next calculated delivery, returned as UTC RFC3339 (`Z`). The server sets it. A schedule change recalculates it.
- `start_date` (String) When this schedule starts. The start day is the calendar date of this instant in `timeZone`, not its UTC date. To start on 2026-11-03 in `America/Los_Angeles`, send `2026-11-03T00:00:00-08:00` (`2026-11-03T08:00:00Z`). A read returns the stored instant as UTC RFC3339 (`Z`).
- `time` (String) Stored instant of the delivery clock, returned as UTC RFC3339 (`Z`). An offset in the request is not preserved. `2026-10-23T10:00:00+02:00` is returned as `2026-10-23T08:00:00Z`. The calendar date is the date of that instant. It is stored and returned, and it is not the subscription start date. Deliveries use only the hour and minute of that instant, interpreted in `timeZone`. Sending `time` already in `Z` makes the next read match the sent date and clock.
- `time_zone` (String) IANA time zone used to calculate deliveries.


<a id="nestedatt--items--subscriptions--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.subscriptions.source`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) ID of the dashboard, report, commitment, alert, or budget. Writable on create and on a patch of a scheduled subscription. On an alert or a budget it is the resource id. Report ids come from `GET /analytics/v1/reports` and `GET /analytics/v1/reports/{id}`. Commitment ids come from `GET /analytics/v1/commitment-manager` and `GET /analytics/v1/commitment-manager/{id}`.
- `name` (String) Display name of the source resource.
